article: [Eligibility for the NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eligibility_for_the_NBA_draft "Eligibility for the NBA draft") The draft is conducted under the eligibility rules established in the league's 2023 [collective bargaining agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_collective_bargaining_agreement "NBA collective bargaining agreement") (CBA) with its players' union. - All drafted players must be at least 19 years old during the calendar year of the draft. In terms of dates, players who were eligible for the 2026 NBA draft must have been born on or before December 31, 2007. - Since the 2016 draft, the following rules are, as implemented by the [NCAA Division I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I "NCAA Division I") council for that division:[\[86\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_NBA_draft#cite_note-123) - Declaration for the draft no longer results in automatic loss of college eligibility. As long as a player does not sign a contract with a professional team outside the NBA or sign with an agent, he retains college eligibility as long as he makes a timely withdrawal from the draft. - NCAA players now have 10 days after the end of the [NBA draft combine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_combine "NBA draft combine") to withdraw from the draft. Since the combine is normally held in mid-May, the current deadline is about five weeks after the previous mid-April deadline. - NCAA players may participate in the draft combine and are allowed to attend one tryout per year with each NBA team without losing college eligibility. - NCAA players may now enter and withdraw from the draft up to two times without loss of eligibility. Previously, the NCAA treated a second declaration of draft eligibility as a permanent loss of college eligibility. ### Early entrants Players who were not automatically eligible had to declare their eligibility for the draft by notifying the NBA offices in writing no later than at least 60 days before the event. For the 2026 draft, the date fell on April 24. Under the CBA a player may withdraw his name from consideration from the draft at any time before the final declaration deadline, which usually falls 10 days before the draft at 5:00 p.m. [EDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") (2100 [UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC "UTC")). Under current NCAA rules, players usually have until 10 days after the draft combine to withdraw from the draft and retain college eligibility. A player who has hired an agent for purposes of negotiating with professional teams[\[b\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_NBA_draft#cite_note-124) retains his remaining college eligibility regardless of whether he is drafted after an evaluation from the NBA Undergraduate Advisory Committee. Players who declare for the NBA draft and are not selected have the opportunity to return to their school for at least another year only after terminating all agreements with their agents,[\[c\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_NBA_draft#cite_note-125) who must have been certified.[\[87\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_NBA_draft#cite_note-126) On April 27, 2026, the NBA announced 71 players (60 college players and 11 international prospects) who filed as early entry candidates.[\[88\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_NBA_draft#cite_note-127) On May 29, 38 early entry candidates withdrew their eligibility.[\[89\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_NBA_draft#cite_note-128) On June 16, three more candidates withdrew their eligibility.[\[90\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_NBA_draft#cite_note-129) #### College underclassmen - They have no remaining college eligibility. - If they graduated from high school in the U.S., but did not enroll in a U.S. college or university, four years have passed since their high school class graduated. - They have signed a contract with a professional basketball team not in the NBA, anywhere in the world, and have played under the contract. Players who meet the criteria for "international" players are automatically eligible if they meet any of the following criteria: - They are at least 22 years old during the calendar year of the draft. In term of dates players born on or before December 31, 2004, are automatically eligible for the 2026 draft. - They have signed a contract with a professional basketball team not in the NBA _within the United States_, and have played under that contract. ## Invited attendees The NBA annually invites players to sit in the so-called "green room", a special room set aside at the draft site for the invited players plus their families and agents. metadata.ogDescription: The 2026 NBA draft is scheduled to be the 80th edition of the National Basketball Association's annual draft. This will be the first draft since 2021 with 60 picks, as no teams have forfeited second-round draft picks for free agency violations. The first round of the draft will be held on June 23, and the second round on June 24.

The [2026 NBA draft](https://www.espn.com/nba/draft/news) is just eight days away (June 23-24, 8 p.m. ET on ABC/ESPN), with the league's withdrawal deadline passing Saturday, and teams and prospects entering the final stretch of meetings and workouts going into [Round 1](https://www.espn.com/nba/draft/rounds).

With the draft picture beginning to crystallize, the intrigue begins at the very top, where the [Washington Wizards](https://www.espn.com/nba/team/_/name/wsh/washington-wizards) have begun to narrow down their options with the No. 1 pick and the [Utah Jazz](https://www.espn.com/nba/team/_/name/utah/utah-jazz) sitting behind them at No. 2. [AJ Dybantsa](http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5142718/aj-dybantsa) and [Darryn Peterson](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5041955/darryn-peterson) remain the projected top two picks, but there's still a question about the order they're selected.

NBA teams continue to await a potential [Giannis Antetokounmpo](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3032977/giannis-antetokounmpo) trade that is expected to have broader ramifications on the draft and offseason. The [Milwaukee Bucks](https://www.espn.com/nba/team/_/name/mil/milwaukee-bucks) have much of the league in a holding pattern as they consider a franchise-changing decision. ESPN's Shams Charania [reported in May](https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48741814/sources-bucks-seeking-trade-offers-giannis-antetokounmpo) that the Bucks were open for business involving the two-time MVP, with a resolution expected prior to the draft.

A lot will play out over the next week as front offices huddle and finalize their boards. Here are my latest draft projections, with new intel from around the NBA shedding light on how things might go. As usual, this mock draft is informed heavily by my conversations with sources around the NBA, in addition to my own evaluations of prospects over the course of the season. These are not my personal rankings, which can be found in [ESPN's top 100](https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46886245/2026-nba-draft-big-board-rankings-top-100-prospects-players).

## First round

![](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/nba/500/was.png&h=110&w=110)

## 1\. [Washington Wizards](https://www.espn.com/nba/team/_/name/wsh/washington-wizards)

**[AJ Dybantsa](http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5142718/aj-dybantsa), SF, [BYU](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/_/id/252/byu-cougars)**

**Freshman**

The Wizards have played their cards close to the vest over the past few weeks, taking their time with the process and evaluating all four candidates atop the draft. Washington has narrowed its focus to Dybantsa and [Darryn Peterson](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5041955/darryn-peterson), sources tell me and Charania.

Peterson has informed the Jazz that he plans to take no further team visits, signaling that he is comfortable with his position and prefers to hear his name called at No. 1 with Washington. He has made himself accessible to the Wizards, previously meeting with them in Los Angeles, and has conducted multiple on-court workouts in front of Washington's decision-makers. Peterson wants to play point guard at the next level, but the presence of [Trae Young](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4277905/trae-young) in Washington is not viewed as an impediment.

Dybantsa visited Washington on Thursday and Friday, and headed from there to Utah on Saturday, his only two planned visits. For months, he has been the favorite around the NBA to hear his name called first, having led Division I in scoring (25.5 PPG), and with his size, physicality and ability to get downhill. Dybantsa has well-documented ties to Utah, after playing his senior year of high school at Utah Prep and last season at BYU, but he also prefers to be the No. 1 pick.

Some around the league believe Dybantsa's profile best aligns with what the Wizards have valued. Last year, they coveted [Ace Bailey](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4873138/ace-bailey), another taller scoring wing. Although Dybantsa plays a much different style, he would check some of the same boxes. Washington's decision will play out over the next eight days.

* * *

![](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/nba/500/utah.png&h=110&w=110)

## 2\. [Utah Jazz](https://www.espn.com/nba/team/_/name/utah/utah-jazz)

**[Darryn Peterson](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5041955/darryn-peterson), PG/SG, [Kansas](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/_/id/2305/kansas-jayhawks)**

**Freshman**

For the past couple of weeks, rival teams have been operating as if Peterson and Dybantsa will be the first two players off the board.

Sources say Peterson's medicals have not raised major concerns with teams, clearing the way for him to hear his name called as a top-two pick. He began the season as ESPN's No. 1 prospect and is the most gifted offensive player in the class. While the season didn't go according to plan at Kansas, where he dealt with [serious cramping issues](https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48710416/darryn-peterson-says-high-doses-creatine-led-cramping), he has always been viewed by teams as a strong candidate for the pick.

Although Peterson does not plan to visit Utah before the draft, that is not considered by rival teams to be a major factor in whether the Jazz will select him. There is precedent for that thinking, as general manager Austin Ainge selected Ace Bailey fifth overall last year, despite Bailey's camp electing not to work out there.

The Jazz are particularly familiar with Dybantsa after he spent the past two years playing in-state. Although his presence creates some positional duplication with Bailey, it would be a major surprise around the NBA if Dybantsa slipped past Utah.

The Jazz are considered to be comfortable with whichever player falls to them, and they have also brought in [Cameron Boozer](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5041935/cameron-boozer) for a visit. While there is support for Boozer in Utah -- as well as the presence of his father Carlos in a front office role -- his fit within a loaded frontcourt that includes [Lauri Markkanen](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4066336/lauri-markkanen), [Jaren Jackson Jr](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4277961/jaren-jackson-jr). and [Walker Kessler](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4433136/walker-kessler) is less clean than the other two options.

Peterson would make for a strong match with the Jazz if available, immediately bolstering their offense and slotting in alongside [Keyonte George](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4433627/keyonte-george) as Utah pushes for playoff contention.

* * *

![](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/nba/500/mem.png&h=110&w=110)

## 3\. [Memphis Grizzlies](https://www.espn.com/nba/team/_/name/mem/memphis-grizzlies)

**[Cameron Boozer](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5041935/cameron-boozer), PF/C, [Duke](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/_/id/150/duke-blue-devils)**

**Freshman**

Since the draft lottery on May 10, the assumption around the NBA has been that Memphis would be thrilled to select Boozer. He is viewed as an excellent match for what the Grizzlies value and holds a strong case as the best player available here. Boozer and [Caleb Wilson](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5095151/caleb-wilson) are both considered candidates, but Boozer's winning résumé and exceptional analytic profile is expected to appeal to Memphis in particular.

Although the way the lottery played out seems likely to slot Boozer third, his addition would be no less massive for the Grizzlies, who moved up from No. 6 to No. 3 in the lottery draw. Boozer would represent a fresh start, with [Ja Morant](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4279888/ja-morant) potentially on the move. His comfort level on the perimeter makes him an intriguing frontcourt partner for [Zach Edey](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4600663/zach-edey), in what could be a standout offensive pairing.

* * *

![](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/nba/500/chi.png&h=110&w=110)

## 4\. [Chicago Bulls](https://www.espn.com/nba/team/_/name/chi/chicago-bulls)

**[Caleb Wilson](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5095151/caleb-wilson), PF/C, [North Carolina](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/_/id/153/north-carolina-tar-heels)**

**Freshman**

Moving up in the lottery (from No. 9) made life quite a bit easier for Chicago's new leadership, led by Bryson Graham. Wilson remains the most likely player to fall to the Bulls, who can sit comfortably at No. 4 and see what unfolds in front of them. He is set to visit Chicago this week and is thought to be happy at the prospect of landing there, where he would immediately become the face of their rebuild and directly address a frontcourt need.

While Wilson doesn't have the same body of work as the three players projected ahead of him, the leap in productivity he took at North Carolina greatly enhanced how teams view his long-term prospects -- his exceptional quickness off the floor and improved motor make him a strong bet to be a high-impact NBA player. As a result, most view this pick as one of the lower-pressure spots and expect it to be a relatively simple decision for Chicago.

* * *

![](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/nba/500/lac.png&h=110&w=110)

## 5\. [LA Clippers](https://www.espn.com/nba/team/_/name/lac/la-clippers) (via Indiana)

**[Keaton Wagler](http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5254165/keaton-wagler), PG/SG, [Illinois](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/_/id/356/illinois-fighting-illini)**

**Freshman**

The next phase of the draft begins at No. 5, where the Clippers are said to be listening to [trade options](https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49011742/nba-draft-2026-six-trade-offers-lottery-giannis-bucks-heat-dybantsa-peterson-boozer-thunder), giving them a different pathway to improve. This pick, obtained from Indiana in the [Ivica Zubac](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4017837/ivica-zubac) trade after it dropped out of the top four, gives LA a valuable chip to replenish its asset cupboard, particularly if it can move back and still select a player with which it feels comfortable. Either way, this draft is an important opportunity for the veteran-heavy Clippers to pivot younger.

Rival teams believe Wagler is among the top options for the Clippers if they make this pick. Last week, he opted to cancel multiple workouts inside the top 10, a sign he feels comfortable with his standing. His versatility and fast-rising trajectory have given him broad appeal with every team in the 5-10 range, and he isn't expected to be on the board long if he falls past No. 5.

The Clippers are said to be looking for a player who can immediately complement the smaller [Darius Garland](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4396907/darius-garland), the key return for [James Harden](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3992/james-harden) at the trade deadline. [Mikel Brown Jr](http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5101761/mikel-brown-jr). and [Brayden Burries](http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5082206/brayden-burries) are two prospects who fit that mold, with Brown scheduled to work out in LA later this week. Of that trio, Wagler best marries long-term upside with immediate rotation value, thanks to his size, shooting and feel as a ball-moving offensive conduit at both backcourt spots.

* * *

![](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/nba/500/bkn.png&h=110&w=110)

## 6\. [Brooklyn Nets](https://www.espn.com/nba/team/_/name/bkn/brooklyn-nets)

**[Darius Acuff Jr](http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5142620/darius-acuff-jr)., PG, [Arkansas](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/_/id/8/arkansas-razorbacks)**

**Freshman**

Brooklyn's pick has been challenging for rival teams to project, with the Nets tied to a large group of prospects and no obvious best fit. Although Acuff doesn't match the Nets' preference for positional size on the perimeter, rival teams have come to view him as a serious candidate.

Acuff appears to have a very narrow draft range, with the Clippers seemingly focused elsewhere and the Nets and Kings viewed as his two primary suitors. He is coming off an excellent season at Arkansas and would immediately become their most talented shot creator. [Mikel Brown Jr](http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5101761/mikel-brown-jr). is another name to watch here.

[Nate Ament](http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5164559/nate-ament)'s size and skill at forward align with how the Nets have drafted in the past, and he is considered by rival teams as a possibility if they opt not to select a guard. However, he is further away from helping a team win, and there is impetus for the Nets to get better immediately, as they don't control their own pick in 2027 and haven't been competitive the past few seasons.

Brooklyn also has a projected $34 million in cap space, although it's unclear how any free agent plans might impact the direction of its draft.

- _**MORE: [Acuff wants to be the next Jalen Brunson, a star with more heart than height](https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49012597/darius-acuff-jr-jalen-brunson-nba-draft-2026)**_


* * *

![](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/nba/500/sac.png&h=110&w=110)

## 7\. [Sacramento Kings](https://www.espn.com/nba/team/_/name/sac/sacramento-kings)

**[Mikel Brown Jr](http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5101761/mikel-brown-jr)., PG, [Louisville](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/_/id/97/louisville-cardinals)**

**Freshman**

Brown appears to be on solid footing going into next week and has had a positive predraft process, putting himself in play above this slot with the Clippers and Nets, and with interest all over the top 10. His size and well-rounded skill set gives him an argument as the ball handler with the highest offensive upside in this second tier of prospects. Teams say he has been impressive in workouts, displaying the deep shooting range and footwork that give him star potential, and helping to assuage concerns around his inconsistent freshman season.

Though Acuff is widely believed to be Sacramento's preferred target, the Kings haven't appeared interested in trading up from No. 7. They are in the early stages of reshuffling the roster under Scott Perry and aren't replete with extra trade assets. They have done plenty of work on the other guards in this range, including Brown and [Kingston Flemings](http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5149077/kingston-flemings), and they appear to be comfortable waiting to see which player falls.

* * *

![](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/nba/500/atl.png&h=110&w=110)

## 8\. [Atlanta Hawks](https://www.espn.com/nba/team/_/name/atl/atlanta-hawks) (via New Orleans)

**[Kingston Flemings](http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5149077/kingston-flemings), PG, [Houston](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/_/id/248/houston-cougars)**

**Freshman**

He is unanimously viewed as a first-round talent and is drawing consideration as high as the teens, but where he ends up might be predicated on how team doctors individually view his case.

This pick should be best-available for the Lakers, who should be focused on the bigger picture of building around [Luka Doncic](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3945274/luka-doncic) but are also dealing with new contracts for [LeBron James](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/1966/lebron-james) and [Austin Reaves](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4066457/austin-reaves). L.A.'s need for a lob option up front would make Quaintance an intriguing addition here.

* * *

![](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/nba/500/den.png&h=110&w=110)

## 26\. [Denver Nuggets](https://www.espn.com/nba/team/_/name/den/denver-nuggets)

**[Koa Peat](http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5041953/koa-peat), PF/SF, [Arizona](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/_/id/12/arizona-wildcats)**

**Freshman**

After opting to stay in the draft rather than return to Arizona, Peat seems to be trending toward the 20s, with teams continuing to express concern about his jump shot. His physicality and defensive versatility might appeal to a team like Denver, which has been able to creatively fit different skill sets around [Nikola Jokic](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3112335/nikola-jokic) and needs to get more athletic along the frontline.

The Nuggets should be taking a best-available approach as they work to improve their depth. They are working with cap constraints as [Peyton Watson](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4576087/peyton-watson) hits restricted free agency, a situation that could lead to Denver moving a veteran player to enable added flexibility.

* * *

![](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/nba/500/bos.png&h=110&w=110)

## 27\. [Boston Celtics](https://www.espn.com/nba/team/_/name/bos/boston-celtics)

**[Meleek Thomas](http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5041951/meleek-thomas), PG/SG, [Arkansas](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/_/id/8/arkansas-razorbacks)**

**Freshman**

After opting to stay in the draft rather than return to Arkansas, Thomas has had a positive predraft process and conducted a wide range of workouts, giving himself a variety of landing spots in the back half of the first round. His size, scoring ability and improving defense have stood out in workout settings and helped him solidify his status in the first.

Boston is a team that annually casts one of the widest nets in predraft workouts and has plenty of depth on the roster, making this pick more of a luxury for them, whether that's picking a more experienced college player or developing a younger talent like Thomas without the pressure of needing to play right away.

* * *

![](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/nba/500/min.png&h=110&w=110)

## 28\. [Minnesota Timberwolves](https://www.espn.com/nba/team/_/name/min/minnesota-timberwolves) (via Detroit)

**[Ebuka Okorie](http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5258459/ebuka-okorie), PG, [Stanford](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/_/id/24/stanford-cardinal)**

**Freshman**

Okorie chose to turn pro rather than return to Stanford and is expected to be called in the first round, but his range appears wide. Some teams love his elusiveness off the dribble and scoring ability, but there are also concerns about his size. The presence of the more established Christian Anderson, Labaron Philon Jr. and Bennett Stirtz creates some depth at point guard, with at least one of those players likely to fall toward the back of the first.

This pick is a potential landing spot for a point guard, with Minnesota needing another ball handler to help [Anthony Edwards](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4594268/anthony-edwards) and create better long-term backcourt depth.

* * *

![](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/nba/500/cle.png&h=110&w=110)

## 29\. [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://www.espn.com/nba/team/_/name/cle/cleveland-cavaliers) (via San Antonio)

**[Tarris Reed Jr.](http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5105809/tarris-reed-jr), C, [UConn](https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/_/id/41/uconn-huskies)**

**Senior**

After making a strong case for himself by putting up three 20-plus-point games in the NCAA tournament, Reed has built momentum on the workout circuit and is trending toward the late first round. His mix of length, physical heft, rebounding instincts and offensive skill make him an appealing plug-and-play role player, and he should appeal to contending teams.

Frontcourt depth is an obvious area of need for the Cavs as they try to maximize their current window, making this an intriguing fit.

* * *

![](https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/nba/500/dal.png&h=110&w=110)

## 30\. [Dallas Mavericks](https://preview.espn.com/nba/team/_/name/dal/dallas-mavericks) (via Oklahoma City)

**Sergio de Larrea, PG/SG, Valencia, Spain**

De Larrea opted to stay in the draft ahead of Saturday's deadline, an indication he has a landing spot most likely in the 25-to-35 range. Teams say de Larrea is open to remaining in Spain next season in the right situation, creating a stash option that could provide cap and roster relief for a first-round team.

He measured officially at 6-foot-6 barefoot with a 6-9 wingspan, giving him massive dimensions for a ball handler, and is coming off a solid season in Spain, where he played a major part on a strong Valencia team and shot just under 40% from 3. Although de Larrea isn't particularly quick, his playmaking feel and positional size give him clear potential to grow into a role.

Although the Mavericks appear ready to start next season with [Kyrie Irving](https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/6442/kyrie-irving) on board, addressing the point guard position in the long run could be an attractive option here.

### 2026 NBA Draft

# 2026 NBA Draft Order: Picks 1-60

Washington won the Draft Lottery and will have the first pick in the 2026 NBA Draft (June 23-24). Here is the offical 1-60 order of selection.

NBA.com Staff

Updated on June 4, 2026 8:43 AM

Watch the full 2026 NBA Draft Lottery drawing from Chicago that resulted in the Washington Wizards receiving the No. 1 overall pick.

The order of selection for the first 14 picks of the **[2026 NBA Draft](https://web.archive.org/web/20250118042223mp_/https://www.nba.com/draft/2026)** was determined by the [2026 NBA Draft Lottery](https://www.nba.com/news/2026-nba-draft-lottery-result) on May 10, with the Washington Wizards, Utah Jazz, Memphis Grizzlies and Chicago Bulls securing the first four picks.

The remaining “lottery teams” are positioned five through 14, in reverse order of their 2025-26 regular-season records.

The complete order of selection of the first round (No. 15-30) and the entire second round (No. 31-60) is determined by reverse order of regular-season record. Each NBA team receives one selection in the first round and one selection in the second round.

Here’s the complete order for the 2026 NBA Draft.

web.markdown:
# NBA Future Draft Pick Details ## Atlanta Hawks Future Traded Pick Details | Year | Incoming | Outgoing | | --- | --- | --- | | 2026 | **2026 first round draft pick from New Orleans**
New Orleans' 2026 1st round pick to Atlanta \[Atlanta-New Orleans, 6/25/2025\]
**2026 second round draft pick from Boston**
Boston's 2026 2nd round pick to Atlanta \[Atlanta-Boston-Brooklyn, 7/7/2025\] | **2026 first round draft pick to San Antonio (swap, Cleveland incoming)**
San Antonio will swap its 2026 1st round pick for Atlanta's 2026 1st round pick and Atlanta will swap the San Antonio pick for Cleveland's 2026 1st round pick \[Atlanta-San Antonio, 6/30/2022; Atlanta-Cleveland, 2/6/2025\]
**2026 second round draft pick to Denver**
Atlanta's 2026 2nd round pick to Denver (via Golden State to Brooklyn) \[Atlanta-Detroit-Golden State-Portland, 2/9/2023; Brooklyn-Golden State, 12/15/2024; Brooklyn-Denver, 2/5/2026\] | | 2027 | **2027 first round draft pick from New Orleans or Milwaukee**
New Orleans will receive the more favorable of its 2027 1st round pick and Milwaukee's 2027 1st round pick and Atlanta will receive the less favorable of the two protected for selections 1-4; if this pick falls within its protected range and is therefore not conveyable, then New Orleans' obligation to Atlanta will be extinguished and New Orleans will instead receive both picks (via New Orleans) \[Denver-Milwaukee-New Orleans-Oklahoma City, 11/23/2020; Atlanta-New Orleans, 7/6/2024\] | **2027 first round draft pick to San Antonio**
Atlanta's 2027 1st round pick to San Antonio \[Atlanta-San Antonio, 6/30/2022\] | | 2028 | **2028 first round draft pick from Utah or Cleveland (less favorable, swap, Atlanta outgoing to Cleveland)**
Utah will receive the more favorable of its 2028 1st round pick and Cleveland's 2028 1st round pick; Atlanta will receive the more favorable of (i) its 2028 1st round pick and (ii) the less favorable of the Utah pick and the Cleveland pick and Cleveland will receive the least favorable of the three (via Utah's right to swap for Cleveland; via Atlanta's right to swap for Utah or Cleveland) \[Cleveland-Utah, 9/3/2022; Atlanta-Cleveland, 2/6/2025\] | **2028 second round draft pick to Brooklyn**
Atlanta's 2028 2nd round pick to Brooklyn (via Golden State) \[Atlanta-Detroit-Golden State-Portland, 2/9/2023; Brooklyn-Golden State, 12/15/2024\] | | 2029 | **2029 second round draft pick from Cleveland**
Cleveland's 2029 2nd round pick to Atlanta \[Atlanta-Cleveland, 2/6/2025\] | **2029 second round draft pick to Charlotte or Oklahoma City**
Charlotte will receive the more favorable of Atlanta's 2029 2nd round pick and Miami's 2029 2nd round pick and Oklahoma City will receive the less favorable of the two (via Oklahoma City) \[Atlanta-Oklahoma City, 9/27/2022; Miami-Oklahoma City, 7/6/2023; Charlotte-Oklahoma City, 2/4/2026\] | | 2030 | **2030 second round draft pick from New York**
New York's 2030 2nd round pick to Atlanta (via Portland) \[New York-Portland, 6/27/2024; Atlanta-Portland, 2/1/2026\] | No picks outgoing. | | 2031 | **2031 second round draft pick from Houston (Atlanta outgoing)**
Atlanta has the right to swap its 2031 2nd round pick for Houston's 2031 2nd round pick protected for selections 56-60 (if this pick falls within its protected range and is therefore not conveyable, then Houston's obligation to Atlanta will be extinguished) \[Atlanta-Brooklyn-Golden State-Houston-L.A. Lakers-Minnesota-Phoenix, 7/6/2025\] | No picks outgoing. | | 2032 | **2032 second round draft pick from L.A. Lakers**
L.A. Lakers' 2032 2nd round pick to Atlanta \[Atlanta-L.A. Lakers, 2/5/2026\] | No picks outgoing. | ## Boston Celtics Future Traded Pick Details | Year | Incoming | Outgoing | | --- | --- | --- | | 2026 | **2026 second round draft pick from Milwaukee**
Milwaukee's 2026 2nd round pick to Boston (via Orlando) \[Milwaukee-Orlando, 11/18/2020; Boston-Orlando, 6/26/2025\] | **2026 second round draft pick to Atlanta**
Boston's 2026 2nd round pick to Atlanta \[Atlanta-Boston-Brooklyn, 7/7/2025\] | | 2027 | No picks incoming. | **2027 second round draft pick to Utah or Charlotte**
Utah will receive the more favorable of Boston's 2027 2nd round pick and Orlando's 2027 2nd round pick and Charlotte will receive the less favorable of the two (via Boston to Orlando to Boston to Utah; via Orlando to Charlotte) \[Boston-Orlando, 3/25/2021; Boston-Orlando, 6/26/2025; Boston-Utah, 8/6/2025; Charlotte-Orlando, 2/4/2026\] | | 2028 | No picks incoming. | **2028 first round draft pick to San Antonio (San Antonio incoming)**
San Antonio has the right to swap its 2028 1st round pick for Boston's 2028 1st round pick protected for selection 1; if this pick falls on its protected selection and is therefore not conveyable, then Boston will instead convey its 2028 2nd round pick to San Antonio protected for selections 46-60 (if this pick falls within its protected range and is therefore not conveyed, then Boston's obligation to San Antonio will be extinguished) \[Boston-San Antonio, 2/10/2022\]
